issues.reason: dim belongs to the intransitive internal-change-of-state class the instruction set names explicitly (stall, weaken, falter, buckle, sag, fade, freeze -> Patient), which it states "is never Agent by default" and which "carries into sealed complements and passives", so (Agent sk_dim_1 stilllight_lantern) is ill-typed - Agent is defined as the volitional doer, which a dimming lantern is not.

new_gaps: Periphrastic causative over an UNACCUSATIVE bare-infinitive complement ("let the lantern dim", "had the beam sag"): the causative bullet assigns the object the caused event's Agent while the intransitive-undergoer split assigns Patient/Theme, and no precedence rule is stated. A licensed form would need to say that the causative bullet fixes only WHICH slot the object fills (the caused event's subject) and that the role of that slot is then set by the ordinary does-it-change test - the causative examples (sprint, sign, leave) are all agentive and never test the collision.
defect_summary: The compliant form is (Patient sk_dim_1 stilllight_lantern) in place of the Agent atom; every other atom in the parse stands.
notes: The reviewer's note that the two bullets collide is correct, but the collision does not license the atom: Agent on a lantern's own dimming fails the role's stated definition, so the doctrinal ambiguity is a gap while the emitted atom is still a defect.
